probes.text: Away on a business trip, Tony keeps noticing a light blinking far off in the darkness outside his hotel window.
At dinner with a table of strangers, Tony talks vaguely about being in the middle of a midlife crisis.

fine_only.text: Tony ends up carrying a briefcase and ID belonging to a travelling salesman who has exactly his face.

probes.text: Chris strong-arms the screenwriter he met in rehab into writing a mob-slasher script to work off his gambling debt.
Chris and his writer pitch their slasher idea to Little Carmine, who hears the title they have settled on.

4.title: The Fleshy Part of the Thigh

probes.text: Johnny is let out of prison for a single day so he can attend his daughter's wedding.
Meadow, interning at a law firm that handles white-collar cases, argues with Finn about how financial criminals are judged.
A man at Chris's addiction recovery meeting passes along a piece of gossip he has heard about a captain.
Vito's car breaks down out of state, leaving him to continue along a country road on foot.
In Los Angeles, Chris discovers a hotel gift lounge where celebrities are handed free luxury items.
Artie confronts Tony for having eaten at a rival restaurant instead of coming to Nuovo Vesuvio.
Chris flies out to the West Coast to cast actors for his mob-slasher movie.
A realtor corners Tony about buying a local store she wants to turn into a Jamba Juice.
Paulie balks at how much the church expects him to donate toward the neighborhood saint's feast.
Rides and stalls fill the street for the neighborhood saint's feast, with Paulie's crew running things.
Nucci chastises Paulie over his handling of the neighborhood feast, and he curses at her.
Janice tearfully thanks Tony over a house arrangement; Carmela comforts her while Tony rolls his eyes behind them.
Melfi suggests that Tony's sister may remind him of their mother, an idea he does not welcome.
Vito, settled into the small town, grows restless and bored with the routine of ordinary daily work.
Carmela travels to Paris with Rosalie, wandering the streets and marveling at the old stone architecture.
Abroad with an old friend, Carmela stands among centuries-old buildings, plainly moved by the city around her.
Little Carmine plays host to a sitdown, hoping to talk the two families back toward peace.
Tony and Carmela drive up to Bobby and Janice's cabin in upstate New York to mark his birthday.
Janice's present is a compilation of old home movies showing Tony as a boy playing with his sisters.
The two couples spend an evening at the lake house drinking heavily and playing Monopoly.
Chris's mob-slasher movie finally has its premiere, and the whole crew turns out to watch it.
Phil marks the birthday of his late brother Billy with a gathering of his own men.
Tony and Paulie kill time together down in Miami, and Paulie's constant talking wears on Tony more each day.
Junior runs a gambling game with the other patients in his psychiatric facility.
Junior strikes up a friendship with a much younger, ill-tempered patient on his ward.
Tony cracks one Jewish joke after another at Hesh's expense while Hesh sits with the crew.
Tony insists on paying Hesh a vig on the loan, even though Hesh never charged him interest.
Vito's widow comes to Tony asking for money so she can move her family somewhere else.
Chris insists he avoids the Bada Bing and Satriale's because being around the alcohol there makes him anxious.
Tony tells Melfi he had been planning to quit therapy, and blames his son's troubles on his own "rotten genes."
In Las Vegas, Tony takes peyote with a stripper and later watches the sun rise over red desert rock.
Tony hits a winning streak at a roulette table, laughing helplessly until he collapses on the casino floor.
Janice tells Tony that Junior's savings have run out and can no longer pay for his facility.
Waiting in a diner booth, Tony flips through the pages of a tabletop jukebox looking for a song.
A pair of Muslim men have been hanging around the Bada Bing, and Tony has taken note of them.
